item.title: Essential Parenting Supports-Parenting Skills Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-08-11

The Administration for Childrens Services intends to renew its contract with Young Adult Institute, Inc. for the continued provision of Essential Parenting Supports parenting skills training program. Young Adult Institute, Inc. headquarters is located at 220 East 42nd Street, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10017. Renewing this program will allow ACS to continue providing year-round parenting skills training and support to parents and caregivers with a suspected cognitive limitation or confirmed Intellectual / Developmental Disabilities (I/DD). Parents referred to the program receive tailored parenting classes, one-on-one parenting coaching, and case management services that connect them to additional support and resources. The renewal term of this contract is October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2029. The renewal total contract amount is $1,798,402.50, and the EPIN is 06823P0006001R001.

This notice is for informational purposes only. Anyone who would like to share comments or concerns regarding the providers performance and other factors relevant to the renewal, may contact Keshia Wyllie via email at keshia.wyllie…

item.title: Alternative to Placement and Aftercare Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $2.7M | Vendor: SCO Family of Services

Pursuant to the Procurement Policy Board Rules, Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii), the Administration for Children's Services seeks to utilize the Negotiated Acquisition Extension procurement method to extend its contract with the SCO Family of Services for Alternative to Placement and Aftercare Services - Juvenile Justice Initiatives - Brooklyn for 11/15/2026 to 6/30/27. The extension period, from November 15, 2026, to June 30, 2027 will provide ACS with sufficient time to finalize a new RFP with an anticipated release on or before July 31, 2026. The resulting award will begin on July 1, 2027. This extension will ensure continuity of services and support ACSs strategic alignment of all ATP contracts to the Citys fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027.

item.title: Alternative to Placement and Aftercare Services Concept Report
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Special Materials | Notice

Through the upcoming RFP, the Division of Youth and Family Justice (DYFJ) will continue its Juvenile Justice Initiative's (JJI) commitment to providing high-quality, evidenced-based interventions for youth at the highest level of need in the juvenile delinquency system - those being recommended for out-of-home placement and those exiting placement and reentering the community.  The upcoming RFP seeks highly experienced service providers to provide both alternative-to-placement (ATP) and placement aftercare services to youth ages 12 to 18 (up to age 17.5 at time of referral) and their families using targeted and specific evidenced-based interventions.  JJI serves youth who have been or are in the process of adjudication in New York City (NYC) juvenile courts. Intensive services allow them to remain at home while receiving support in the community, instead of being remanded to a juvenile justice setting. JJI services can be put in place for youth when leaving a juvenile justice non-secure or limited secure placement and transitioning back to the community. item.title: In-Person/VRI interpretation for Spoken Languages Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $9.0M | Vendor: Legal Interpreting Services Inc.

The Immigrant Services and Language Affairs (ISLA) division of The NYC Administration for Childrens Services (ACS) is seeking three vendors to provide In-Person/VRI interpretation for Spoken Languages, Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing Interpretation and Language services, and Written Translation Services. This Procurement will assist ACS compliance with Local Law 73 (2003), Local Law 30 (2017), the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II, and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which require ACS and its network of providers to provide interpretation and translation services for all limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families to enable equal access to ACS services, as well as ensure best practice for casework with limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families. The term of each of the contracts will be July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2029.

item.title: Workforce Development Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $7.4M | Vendor: Youth Justice Network Inc.

Workforce Development Services will offer high-quality education and/or training programs to youth to promote opportunities for successful career development. Focusing on a holistic approach, these activities will enable youth to expand and develop competencies to realize their career interests and promote pathways to pursue them. This will also help youth market their skills and qualifications and provide youth with social and emotional support to build life skills, identify aptitudes and interests, set academic and career goals, facilitate connections to programs/services that support goal attainment, and plan for successful transitions from the juvenile justice system.

item.title: Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing Language Access Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $685K | Vendor: American Sign Language Inc

The Immigrant Services and Language Affairs (ISLA) division of The NYC Administration for Childrens Services (ACS) is seeking a vendor to provide sign language interpretation services. Services needed are In-person Sign Language interpretation, On-Site Sign Language interpretation, and on-demand video remote interpretation for American Sign Language (ASL), Certified Deaf Interpretation (CDI), Foreign Sign Language, and Communication Access Realtime Translation (CART) Services. This Procurement will assist ACS compliance with Local Law 73 (2003), Local Law 30 (2017), the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II, and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which require ACS and its network of providers to provide interpretation and translation services for all limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families to enable equal access to ACS services, as well as ensure best practice for casework with limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families. The term of each of the contract will be July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2029.
